references.label: Hutchinson 2016 RESCUEicp
references.citation: Hutchinson PJ, Kolias AG, Timofeev IS, et al. Trial of decompressive craniectomy for traumatic intracranial hypertension. N Engl J Med. 2016;375(12):1119-1130.
references.excerpt: At 6 months, decompressive craniectomy in patients with traumatic brain injury and refractory intracranial hypertension resulted in lower mortality and higher rates of vegetative state, lower severe disability, and upper severe disability than medical care. The rates of moderate disability and good recovery were similar in the two groups.

references.excerpt: In critically ill patients with traumatic brain injury and anemia, a liberal transfusion strategy did not reduce the risk of an unfavorable neurologic outcome at 6 months.

references.label: Taccone 2024 TRAIN
references.citation: Taccone FS, Rynkowski CB, Møller K, et al. Restrictive vs liberal transfusion strategy in patients with acute brain injury: the TRAIN randomized clinical trial. JAMA. 2024;332(19):1623-1633.
references.excerpt: Patients with acute brain injury and anemia randomized to a liberal transfusion strategy were less likely to have an unfavorable neurological outcome than those randomized to a restrictive strategy.

references.excerpt: The panel recommends EEG in generalized convulsive status epilepticus and to rule out nonconvulsive seizures in brain-injured patients and in comatose ICU patients without primary brain injury who have unexplained and persistent altered consciousness. references.excerpt: If the apnoea test targets are not met (start PaCO2 ≥ 5.3 kPa, minimum 5 minutes, end PaCO2 ≥ 8.0 kPa, rise PaCO2 ≥ 2.7 kPa, end pH <7.3) ... This would ordinarily be at the time of completion of the second set of clinical tests. This becomes the recorded time of death.

references.label: GBS anaesthesia SNACC
references.citation: SNACC. A Review of Guillain-Barre Syndrome. Spring Newsletter 2016. Accessed 30 October 2026.
references.excerpt: Succinylcholine is avoided in view of the denervated skeletal muscles and the risk of hyperkalemia.

references.label: GBS respiratory review
references.citation: Leonhard SE, et al. Diagnosis and management of Guillain–Barré syndrome in ten steps. Nat Rev Neurol. 2019;15:671–683. Step 8. Accessed 30 October 2026.

references.reviewNote: Neurological deficits involving SCI/peripheral nerve injury: potassium release relates to extent of paralysis. Product-specific periods do not establish a universally safe first 48 hours or recovery at 9/12 months.

cards.question: What are the CPP and ICP targets in severe traumatic brain injury?
cards.answer: Aim for ICP <22 mmHg and CPP 60–70 mmHg (BTF 2016); avoid CPP >70 mmHg with fluid/pressor to prevent ARDS, and avoid CPP <50 mmHg which risks ischaemia.

cards.question: How are tier-3 interventions for refractory raised ICP escalated?
cards.answer: After head-up, sedation, paralysis, CSF drainage and osmotherapy: consider barbiturate coma (thiopentone burst-suppression on EEG), moderate hypothermia (35–36 °C) or decompressive craniectomy (RESCUEicp showed reduced mortality but more vegetative survival).

cards.question: When should hypertonic saline be preferred over mannitol?
cards.answer: Hypertonic saline is preferred in hypovolaemia, hyponatraemia or established renal impairment; mannitol is contraindicated if serum osmolality >320 mOsm/kg or oliguria. Both reduce ICP via osmotic gradients but HTS also expands intravascular volume.
